introduction: This advanced level analyzes the mechanisms of parliamentary oversight via Financial Committees, the various tools (Motions) used to hold the executive accountable, Parliamentary Privileges, and the Anti-Defection Law.

core_concepts.title: Public Accounts Committee (PAC)
core_concepts.description: The oldest financial committee, created in 1921. It has 22 members (15 from LS + 7 from RS). It audits the reports of the CAG. By convention, its chairman is from the Opposition.

core_concepts.title: Estimates Committee
core_concepts.description: The largest committee with 30 members. ALL members are exclusively from the Lok Sabha. It examines budget estimates and suggests economies in public expenditure.

core_concepts.title: Important Motions
core_concepts.description: 1. No-Confidence Motion: Needs support of 50 members to be admitted; if passed, the entire cabinet must resign. 2. Adjournment Motion: Introduced to draw attention to a matter of urgent public importance. 3. Censure Motion: Moved against an individual minister or group for specific policies.

core_concepts.title: Zero Hour vs. Question Hour
core_concepts.description: Question Hour is the first hour of a sitting. Zero Hour immediately follows it and is an informal device (an Indian innovation since 1962, not mentioned in rules) where MPs can raise matters without prior notice.

core_concepts.title: Anti-Defection Law (10th Schedule)
core_concepts.description: Added by the 52nd Amendment Act (1985). It disqualifies MPs/MLAs for defection. The deciding authority is the Presiding Officer of the House. Originally exempt from judicial review, the SC ruled in the Kihoto Hollohan case (1992) that the Speaker's decision IS subject to judicial review.

important_entities.name: Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG)
important_entities.significance: Acts as a 'friend, philosopher, and guide' to the Public Accounts Committee in examining public expenditure.

important_entities.name: Leader of Opposition
important_entities.significance: The leader of the largest opposition party having not less than one-tenth (10%) of the total seats of the House is recognized as the Leader of Opposition, enjoying the rank of a cabinet minister.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Do not mix up committee memberships. The PAC and COPU (Committee on Public Undertakings) have members from BOTH houses (15+7). The Estimates Committee has NO representation from the Rajya Sabha.

A Censure motion can be moved against an individual minister and requires specific reasons. A No-Confidence motion is moved against the ENTIRE council of ministers and does NOT need to state the reasons for its adoption.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: Estimates is Exclusive, PAC is a Pack
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Estimates committee is 'Exclusive' to Lok Sabha (30). PAC is a 'Pack' of both houses (15 LS + 7 RS = 22).

exam_strategy_tips: In Assertion-Reasoning questions, perfectly align the 'Anti-Defection Law' and the 'Kihoto Hollohan Case' regarding judicial review.
UPSC frequently tests the difference between Starred Questions (requires oral answer, supplementaries allowed) and Unstarred Questions (written answer, no supplementaries) during Question Hour.
